title: PersonaEvaluationScenario
description: One fixed evaluation scenario for MIND's persona evaluation harness. Every scenario in eval/personas/, regardless of persona (Developer, Manager, Higher Manager, Field Engineer, Salesperson, CEO), MUST conform to this single schema. Only the values differ between personas — never the structure.

scenario_id.description: Unique identifier for this scenario across the whole eval/personas/ set. Convention: <role>_<seniority?>_<short_slug>, e.g. developer_junior_late_pr_review.

tasks.description: The candidate tasks the persona is choosing between in this scenario. Must include at least one task other than the expected answer, so the scenario actually tests a choice.

expected_top_task_id.description: The task_id (from `tasks`) that a correct model must pick as the single best use of the persona's free time in this context. Invariant enforced by the harness validator, not by this JSON Schema: this value must equal the task_id of exactly one entry in `tasks`.

expected_reason.description: Short, checkable, data-grounded explanation of why expected_top_task_id is correct, referencing concrete fields from context/tasks (deadline, free_time_minutes, blocked, tier...). Must not be a vague preference statement.

role.description: Who the user is, in terms the system cares about (see MIND-01-System-Overview.md role table). Same six values across the whole persona set.

seniority.description: Optional. Only set when seniority genuinely changes the correct answer for this scenario (e.g. a Junior Developer is not expected to pick up an architecture-review task a Senior would). Omit or null when it would not change the expected answer.

department.description: Optional, nullable. Some roles (e.g. CEO) are not scoped to a single department; leave null rather than forcing a value.

free_time_minutes.description: How much free time the persona has right now. The single most load-bearing field in the scenario — the same task list can have a different correct answer at 20 minutes vs. 120 minutes.

current_datetime.description: ISO 8601 timestamp establishing 'now' for this scenario, so task.deadline can be evaluated as near/far/passed.

time_horizon.description: The window the persona is planning within. A CEO scenario will typically use a wider horizon than a Developer scenario, per the role/timescale table in MIND-01-System-Overview.md.

constraints.description: Any additional situational constraint the model must know about to answer correctly (e.g. 'no meetings can be scheduled', 'must be done without manager approval'). Empty array when there are none — do not omit the key.

task_id.description: Unique within this scenario. Referenced by dependencies and by expected_top_task_id.

description.description: Enough detail that a model (and a human reader) can judge duration, urgency and relevance without outside knowledge.

deadline.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, or null if the task has no hard deadline. Evaluated against context.current_datetime.

estimated_duration_minutes.description: How long the task takes. Compared directly against context.free_time_minutes.

tier.description: What KIND of task this is — independent of persona. A Developer can receive an Operational or a Tactical task; tier is not implied by role. See 'Tier vs. Persona' in SCHEMA.md.

blocked.description: True if this task cannot currently be worked on (e.g. waiting on a dependency). A blocked task should generally not be the expected_top_task_id.

dependencies.description: task_ids (within this same scenario) that must complete before this task can start. Empty array if none — do not omit the key.

type.description: Where this scenario came from. 'real' = hand-written from a genuine (non-Gong) situation; 'AMI'/'FUNSD' = derived from those public corpora; 'synthetic' = fabricated for coverage; 'other' = anything else, explained in source_detail.

source_detail.description: Free-text pointer to the concrete origin (e.g. an AMI meeting ID, or 'other' explanation). Required in practice when type is 'AMI', 'FUNSD', or 'other'; optional otherwise.
